Retrieved via Exa 19 July 2026. Straits Times carrying a Reuters investigation (sourcing is Reuters newsroom; NB straitstimes.com not on approved list - use Reuters URL if available, else treat as Reuters wire).

SUNDAY 19 JULY (Reuters investigation):
- Delayed orders from senior military commanders, lack of basic equipment and overall confusion hindered Venezuelan troop deployment in the crucial first days after two devastating earthquakes struck the country's Caribbean coast in June; about 5,000 people died (toll tops 5,000). Eight sources familiar with the response told Reuters.
- Acting President Delcy Rodriguez (backed by Trump) defended the government's response amid criticism that personnel arrived late and did little to help victims, including people trapped in rubble.
- Overlapping authority: Rodriguez named National Guard commander Juan Sulbaran Quintero "single authority" while also decreeing powers to Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, creating confusion over who directed operations.
NOTE: This is a follow-up investigation of a June disaster, not a fresh weekend event. Lower priority; use only if a slot needs filling.
